chunks: Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Ubayda, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man from us who buys from the Sultan from the camels of charity and the sheep of charity, while he knows that they take from the people more than the right which is obligatory upon them. He said, so he said: 'The camels and sheep are no different than the wheat and the barley and other than that; there is no problem with it until you recognize the prohibited [part] with your own eye.'

It was said to him: 'So what do you think regarding a charity collector who comes to us and takes the charities of our sheep, so we say to him, 'Sell them to us,' and he sells them to us. So what do you think regarding buying them from him?' He said: 'If he has taken them and segregated them, then there is no problem.'

It was said to him: 'So what do you think regarding the wheat and the barley? The apportioner comes to us, so he apportions our share and takes his share and segregates it with a measure. So what do you think regarding buying that foodstuff from him?' He said: 'If he had taken possession of it with a measure, and you were present during that measurement, then there is no problem with buying it from him without measuring it.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to buy Zakat goods from the government if they have over-collected from the people?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) establishes that purchasing Zakat assets from the Sultan or collectors is permissible even if they have usurped excess amounts, provided the specific goods have been segregated and taken into their possession (qabd). For grain, the transaction is valid if the buyer witnessed the initial measurement, reflecting the Shia juristic principle that the ruler's possession validates the asset despite potential irregularities in collection. This ruling underscores the distinction between the illegitimacy of the exaction and the validity of the subsequent sale of the physical goods.

en.hubeali:
Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Abu Ubeyda, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the man from us buying from the Sultan (ruling authority), from the camels of charity (Zakat) and sheep of charity (Zakat), and he knew that they are taking from them (masses) more than the rightful which is obligated upon them. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The camel and sheep are likes of the wheat and the barley, and other than that. There is no problem with it until he recognises the Prohibition exactly’. 
It was said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘So what is your<sup>asws</sup> view regarding a charity (Zakat) collector who comes to us, so he takes the charities (Zakat) of our sheep. So we are saying, ‘Sell these back to us’. So what is your<sup>asws</sup> view regarding buying these from him?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If he has taken them (away) and segregated them, so there is no problem’. 
It was said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘So what is your<sup>asws</sup> view regarding the wheat and the barley. The apportioner (for charity) comes to us, so he apportions our share, and he takes his share and segregates it with a measurement. So what is your<sup>asws</sup> view regarding buying that foodstuff from him?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If he had taken possession of it with a measurement, and you were present during that measurement, so there is no problem with buying it from him without measuring it (again)’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ibn Mahbub has narrated from Hisham ibn Salim from abu ‘Ubayd who has said the following: “I once asked abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of one of our men who bought from the sultan of the camels of charity and sheep of charity and he knew that they took more than what is rightly due on them. He (the Imam) said, ‘Camels and sheep are just like wheat and barley and other goods. It is not unlawful unless he recognizes the very substance of what is unlawful.’

It was asked, ‘What do you say about the charity collectors who come to us, collect the charity from our sheep, then we ask them to sell them to us and they sell them? What do you say about buying from them? He (the Imam) said, ‘If he has taken them away, then it is not unlawful.’
It was asked, ‘What do you say about wheat and barley which the charity collector takes from us with his measurement and keeps it to one side: if we buy such foodstuff from him?’
He (the Imam) said, ‘If he has taken possession with a certain measurement, then it is not unlawful to buy from him without measuring.”
